DAY 01

You Are Already Allowed to Be Near

THE DAY’S THOUGHT

Beginning something as important as faith can make you painfully aware of everything you do not yet know. You may hear Arabic words you cannot understand. You may watch someone pray effortlessly while you are still trying to remember what comes next. It can create the strange feeling that everyone else is somehow closer to Allah because they know more.

But when Allah speaks about those who call upon Him in the Qur’an, He says simply, “I am near.” There is no qualification attached to that nearness saying you must first know enough, speak Arabic beautifully, or understand every part of your new faith.

You can come to Allah while you are still learning.

You can come confused.

You can come grateful.

You can come with questions.

Your relationship with Allah does not begin when you finally feel like a knowledgeable Muslim.

It has already begun.

Qur’an 2:186

text:
ONE THING TO LEARN

Du’a
دُعَاء

Du’a means supplication or calling upon Allah. Unlike salah, which is the formal ritual prayer, du’a is your personal turning toward Allah. You can ask for help, give thanks, seek forgiveness, express fear, or simply bring what is in your heart before Him.

Outside the formal prayer, your du’a does not need to be in Arabic. Allah understands the words you speak and everything you struggle to put into words.

You do not need to know everything before you begin speaking to Allah.

Du’a can begin before you know exactly what to say.

Sometimes turning toward Allah is already the beginning.
